value.body: Research associates support research projects at universities, institutes, labs and NGOs, working under a lead researcher or principal investigator. Depending on the field, the day involves running experiments or surveys, collecting and analysing data, reviewing literature and helping write papers and reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: A bachelor's or master's in the subject; many posts ask for a master's

items.label: Common funding
items.value: Project grants (e.g. DST, DBT, ICSSR, CSIR), so posts are often fixed-term

items.label: Related titles
items.value: Research assistant, project assistant, junior research fellow (JRF)

items.label: India's R&D spending (GERD)
items.source: DST, R&D Statistics at a Glance 2022-23

items.label: Share of GERD from central government
items.note: Private industry ~36%; much research hiring runs on public grants

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually apply to advertised project posts at universities and institutes, which list the required degree and are tied to a grant. Qualifying CSIR-UGC NET or UGC-NET for a JRF, or a GATE score in science fields, opens funded fellowships that can lead to a PhD.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Lab, field or survey data collection
Data analysis in Excel, R, SPSS or Python

value.title: At a glance
items: Many posts are contract-based and end with the project.
Common next steps: PhD, a fellowship, or research roles in industry or NGOs.
Lab sciences and social sciences differ a lot in daily work.
